subject: Aligning telemetry scope & role definitions for DPA execution
messages:
From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acme.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Initial DPA redline + telemetry questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for sending over the DPA. Acme's legal team went through v2 and we have two high-level open items before we can execute:

1) Role mapping for inference artifacts: we need a short statement that clarifies whether embeddings and inference logs (including KV cache/telemetry) are treated as controller data or processor telemetry. Our compliance team is nervous about embeddings being considered "telemetry" if they can be reconstituted.

2) Subprocessor transparency & transfers: we saw a different subprocessor list on your console. Can you confirm the current list for EU-hosted workloads and whether SCCs + UK Addendum will be applied for transfers?

Attached is Acme's annotated redline (redline_dpa_Acme_v3.pdf) and a short questionnaire on log retention. We prefer a 30-day retention window for request-level logs and that any long-term analytics be aggregated/pseudonymized.

Proposed next step: can your legal/infosec team provide a one-page note on telemetry scope and a finalized subprocessor CSV? We can then route to procurement for DocuSign.

Best,
Samantha Liu
Senior Counsel, Acme Corporation

Attachment: redline_dpa_Acme_v3.pdf (PDF, 245KB)

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + telemetry questions

Samantha — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. High level response to your two bullets:

- Role mapping: Redwood acknowledges Acme as the Controller and Redwood as the Processor for customer-provided data used to fulfill API requests. For telemetry, we propose splitting into two buckets: (a) request-level logs (request headers and payload excerpts) that are retained for operational troubleshooting and will be treated as "processor operational logs" with a default 30-day retention for EU-hosted accounts; (b) aggregated telemetry (latency histograms, sampling-based anomaly metrics, model quality metrics derived from prompt sets) that we retain in aggregated/pseudonymized form for product improvement.

We are uncomfortable with any position that classifies embeddings as "only telemetry" when the customer provides embedding input that must be persisted to deliver their application. To address Acme's concern, we propose the following clause: "Customer-provided embeddings and vectors are Customer Data. Processor telemetry excludes re-identifiable embeddings; where Processor requires temporary feature-caches to service requests, those caches will be cleared within the agreed retention window and not used for model re-training without Customer consent."

- Subprocessors & transfers: I've requested an export of the current EU subprocessor list and a note on transfer mechanisms. Our standard is to use SCCs for EU transfers and apply the UK Addendum where applicable; for accounts that require, we can include a written commitment in the DPA.

Next steps: Laura will distribute an internal one-pager and the subprocessor CSV to you by EOD tomorrow. If that works for Acme, we can prepare the DocuSign packet.

Cheers,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + telemetry questions — internal note + attachments

Samantha / Priyom — attaching the items we promised. Quick summary for the record:

- Attached: subprocessor_list_202611.pdf (current list for EU region) and a short Telemetry Scope Note (pasted below).

Telemetry Scope Note (summary):
- Customer Data: any text, files, or vectors that Customer submits and tags for persistence (including embeddings stored by Customer under their account)
- Operational Logs (Processor Operational Logs): ephemeral request logs (headers, routing, timestamps, truncated payloads) retained 30 days; stored encrypted at rest; accessible to Customer on reasonable request for troubleshooting
- Aggregated Telemetry: metrics and sampled telemetry used to improve platform reliability and performance; kept in aggregate and with standard pseudonymization; not linked to Customer identity for product usage analysis unless explicitly authorized

Redlines we accept: limited — we will include the KR clause about not using Customer-provided embeddings for model training without consent; we will add an explicit SCC + UK Addendum commitment for EU accounts. Items we need to hold on: blanket deletion requests that would prevent us from reasonable operational debugging (we can offer a narrower deletion scope).

Attachments: subprocessor_list_202611.pdf (PDF, 78KB)

Laura Bennett
Head of Privacy & Contracts, Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessor_list_202611.pdf (PDF, 78KB)

From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acme.com>

Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 16:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + telemetry questions — ready to sign

Laura / Priyom,

Thanks — the telemetry note and the subprocessor list address the majority of our concerns. A few follow-ups but minor:
- We appreciate the explicit "no training without consent" clause for embeddings. Please add a simple sentence that any temporary caches used for request routing are cleared within 30 days and cannot be exported to third parties.
- Procurement wants DocuSign with the SCC Annex included. Please send the signing packet and reference HS-239482 in the DocuSign message so our procurement system picks up the record.

If you can add the cache-clear sentence and send the DocuSign link with HS-239482 by EOD, we will route for signature and expect execution within 48 hours.

Sincerely,
Samantha Liu
Senior Counsel, Acme Corporation
